facts.text: Circle City, Arizona was built in the late 1950s by The Workmen's Circle, a Jewish fraternal society with socialist roots.
The Workmen's Circle, founded in the early 20th century, carried socialist ideals into its community planning.
The town was designed as a retirement community for its aging members, offering a peaceful place to settle.
Circle City welcomed anyone over fifty to live there, expanding its age‑friendly vision beyond its founding members.
The community embraced people of all races and religions long before the Fair Housing Act, setting a progressive precedent.
This inclusive policy began a decade earlier than the 1968 Fair Housing Act, highlighting Circle City's forward‑thinking spirit.
